ok.name: lecture-gf-lesion
ok.title: Giant Fiber Lesion: Visual vs Tactile Escape
ok.description: Pedagogical walkthrough comparing visual looming vs mechanosensory escape under giant fiber lesion.

steps.title: 1. Dual Parallel Escape Pathways
steps.explanation: Drosophila uses parallel escape pathways: fast visual escape via the giant fiber (DNp01), and tactile escape via antennal/leg mechanoreceptors through non-giant DNs.
steps.key_takeaway: Parallel neural circuits mediate escape from looming shadows vs physical touch.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Hampel et al. 2015, eLife 4:e08758

steps.title: 2. Silencing the Giant Fiber (DNp01 Lesion)
steps.explanation: Silencing DNp01 severs the direct link from looming detectors to thoracic jump motor neurons.
steps.key_takeaway: DNp01 lesion selectively disables the visual looming escape circuit.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962

steps.title: 3. Looming Visual Cue (Fails)
steps.explanation: With DNp01 silenced, an optical looming stimulus excites LPLC2/LC4, but the signal cannot reach motor neurons. Escape jump fails.
steps.key_takeaway: Visual looming stimuli fail to trigger escape when DNp01 is silenced.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962

neurons.label: LPLC2 + LC4
neurons.role: Active detectors blocked by severed DNp01

steps.title: 4. Tactile Mechanosensory Cue (Preserved)
steps.explanation: Presenting tactile air puff / touch to antennae (JO-C/E) recruits alternative non-giant descending pathways. Tactile escape remains fully functional.
steps.key_takeaway: Non-giant tactile escape pathways remain completely functional despite DNp01 ablation.
steps.citation: Hampel et al. 2015, eLife 4:e08758; Allen et al. 2006, J Neurosci 26:1565

ok.name: lecture-looming
ok.title: Looming Visual Escape Circuit
ok.description: Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila looming escape from retina to giant fiber.

steps.title: 1. Spontaneous Baseline State
steps.explanation: Resting activity across optic lobe visual projection neurons and descending motor pathways is calm (~5-8 Hz baseline spontaneous firing). Inhibitory and excitatory inputs maintain homeostatic equilibrium.
steps.key_takeaway: Baseline state is calm stochastic firing without premature escape trigger.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Ache et al. 2019, Curr Biol 29:1073

neurons.label: LPLC2 + LC4
neurons.role: Visual projection neurons sensitive to optical expansion

steps.title: 2. Expanding Retinal Loom Detection
steps.explanation: An approaching threat expands on the retina. LPLC2 and LC4 compute non-linear angular expansion rates and fire high-frequency action potentials.
steps.key_takeaway: LPLC2 and LC4 selectively encode optical looming expansion.

neurons.label: LPLC2, LC4
neurons.role: Visual detectors driven by looming edge expansion

steps.title: 3. Synaptic Convergence onto Giant Fiber
steps.explanation: LPLC2 and LC4 terminate directly in the posterior slope, forming hundreds of chemical synapses onto giant dendrites of descending neuron DNp01.
steps.key_takeaway: Summation of hundreds of inputs rapidly depolarizes DNp01 toward firing threshold.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962

neurons.label: DNp01
neurons.role: Giant fiber receiving posterior slope synaptic convergence

steps.title: 4. Escape Jump Motor Readout
steps.explanation: Once DNp01 fires, its action potential propagates down the cervical connective into the thoracic ganglion, activating tergotrochanteral motor neurons.
steps.key_takeaway: DNp01 activation triggers an unguided, explosive jump takeoff in <5 ms.
steps.citation: von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Allen et al. 2006, J Neurosci 26:1565

ok.name: lecture-moonwalker
ok.title: Moonwalker Backward Walking Circuit
ok.description: Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila backward walking coordination by MDN.

steps.title: 1. Forward Walking Default State
steps.explanation: In foraging flies, descending neurons like DNp09 promote forward walking, driving tripod leg motor patterns.
steps.key_takeaway: Forward locomotion is driven by forward-promoting descending command neurons.
steps.citation: Bidaye et al. 2014, Science 344:97; Bidaye et al. 2020, Neuron 108:109

steps.title: 2. Collision & MDN Activation
steps.explanation: Physical obstacles or mechanosensory antennal touch activate the bilateral pair of Moonwalker Descending Neurons (MDN).
steps.key_takeaway: Obstacle collision rapidly excites MDN command neurons.

neurons.label: MDN
neurons.role: Bilateral descending neurons directing backward walking

steps.title: 3. Stepping Rhythm Inversion
steps.explanation: MDN simultaneously inhibits forward walking central pattern generators and activates backward motor rhythms, inverting stepping phase.
steps.key_takeaway: MDN acts as an executive toggle switching gait polarity.
steps.citation: Bidaye et al. 2014, Science 344:97; Feng et al. 2020, Nature 585:395

ok.name: lecture-sugar
ok.title: Sugar Gustatory Pathway & Proboscis Extension
ok.description: Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila sugar taste sensing and feeding reflex.

steps.title: 1. Gustatory Detection by Sugar Receptors
steps.explanation: Sucrose contact excites gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs) on labellum and tarsi, sending action potentials into the subesophageal zone.
steps.key_takeaway: Sugar contact activates gustatory sensory neurons innervating the SEZ.
steps.citation: Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210; Yao & Scott 2022, Cell 185:2472

steps.title: 2. Relay via Sugar SEL Projection Neurons
steps.explanation: Sugar sensory afferents synapse onto subesophageal layer projection neurons (Sugar SEL PNs: GNG540/GNG550), relaying excitation to motor command pools.
steps.key_takeaway: Sugar SEL PNs relay taste signals to feeding motor circuits.
steps.citation: Yao & Scott 2022, Cell 185:2472; Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210

steps.title: 3. Motor Neuron 9 (MN9) Proboscis Extension
steps.explanation: Excitatory signals reach MN9, innervating the retractor bulbi muscle to trigger the Proboscis Extension Response (PER). Bitter taste pathways do not excite MN9.
steps.key_takeaway: MN9 drives proboscis extension; bitter inputs fail to activate MN9.
steps.citation: Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210; Schwarz et al. 2017, eLife 6:e19892

ok.name: lecture-tmaze
ok.title: Mushroom Body Olfactory Conditioning
ok.description: Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila olfactory associative learning in the mushroom body.

steps.title: 1. Sparse Odor Encoding by Kenyon Cells
steps.explanation: Antennal lobe projection neurons diverge onto ~2,000 intrinsic Kenyon Cells (KCs). Odors activate sparse, decorrelated ~5% subsets of KCs in the mushroom body calyx.
steps.key_takeaway: Kenyon cells form sparse, distinct odor representations.
steps.citation: Aso et al. 2014, eLife 3:e04577; Turner et al. 2008, Nature 454:493

steps.title: 2. Dopaminergic Reinforcement (PPL1 / Electric Shock)
steps.explanation: Pairing CS+ odor with electric shock recruits PPL1 dopaminergic neurons, releasing dopamine coincident with active Kenyon cell presynaptic boutons.
steps.key_takeaway: PPL1 DANs signal negative reinforcement to specific mushroom body compartments.
steps.citation: Claridge-Chang et al. 2009, Cell 139:405; Aso et al. 2014, eLife 3:e04577

steps.title: 3. Long-Term Depression at KC-to-MBON Synapses
steps.explanation: Coincident KC spikes and dopamine drive selective long-term depression (LTD) of synapses from active KCs onto approach-directing MBONs.
steps.key_takeaway: LTD of approach MBONs tips circuit balance toward avoidance.
steps.citation: Hige et al. 2015, Neuron 88:985; Owald & Waddell 2015, Curr Opin Neurobiol 35:178

neurons.label: Mushroom Body Output Neurons
neurons.role: Readout neurons projecting to motor systems

steps.title: 4. Memory Recall & T-Maze Choice
steps.explanation: At the choice point, CS+ odor evokes depressed approach MBON firing. Unbalanced avoidance signals steer the fly into the safe odor arm.
steps.key_takeaway: Flies avoid the shock-paired odor with statistically significant avoidance (PI > 0.5).
steps.citation: Tully & Quinn 1985, J Comp Physiol A 157:263
